headline.headline: CROW-ARMSTRONG BLASTS NO. 22 IN TENTH AS CUBS ESCAPE PITTSBURGH, 3-2
headline.deck: Chicago outfielder's home run in extras lifts Cubs past Pirates in ten-inning thriller
headline.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Pete Crow-Armstrong delivered when the Cubs needed him most, crushing his 22nd home run of the season in the tenth inning Friday night to break a 2-2 tie and send Chicago past the Pittsburgh Pirates, 3-2, at PNC Park before 35,593 fans.

The game was a grinding, low-scoring affair through nine innings, with Pittsburgh scratching out a run in the fifth and the Cubs answering in the sixth to level the score at one apiece. The Pirates pushed across another run to take a 2-1 edge, before Chicago tied it again to force extra innings. Crow-Armstrong, who also doubled on the night, gave reliever Matthew Boyd the winning decision when the Cubs plated two runs in the tenth to Pittsburgh's one, sealing the 3-2 final.

Boyd earned the win on the mound as Chicago rode Crow-Armstrong's big stick out of western Pennsylvania with a victory. The young outfielder's 22-homer season continues to turn heads across the National League, and Friday's extra-inning shot was the signature swing of a contest that neither bullpen wanted to surrender.

secondary.headline: YANKEES EDGE PHILLIES, 1-0, IN TENSE BATTLE AT CITIZENS BANK PARK
secondary.deck: New York scores lone run in fourth inning, holds Philadelphia scoreless in front of 43,165
secondary.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The New York Yankees scratched out the game's only run in the fourth inning Friday and never looked back, blanking the Philadelphia Phillies, 1-0, before a packed house of 43,165 at Citizens Bank Park. The game featured a parade of hit batsmen, with Adrian Sanchez, McMahon, and Rincones Jr. all taking pitches off the body at various points, and the tension never fully dissipated through nine frames.

Jesus Luzardo took a hit-by-pitch decision against him when he plunked Sanchez, while Jose Alvarado drilled McMahon and Schlittler caught Rincones Jr. New York's pitching staff was otherwise immaculate, protecting the slim lead from the fourth inning on and handing Philadelphia yet another shutout loss in a game the Phillies had every opportunity to escape differently.

secondary.headline: MAHOMES CLEARED FULLY FOR CAMP, CHIEFS SIGNAL BIG MAN IS BACK
secondary.deck: Kansas City quarterback declares himself 'amazing' after recovering from knee surgery
secondary.body:
KANSAS CITY -- Patrick Mahomes has been fully cleared to participate in training camp after undergoing knee surgery following the 2025 season, the Chiefs announced Friday, with the quarterback himself declaring he feels "amazing" heading into the summer. The news removes the last significant question mark hanging over Kansas City's roster as camp opens and the franchise prepares to contend again in the AFC.

Mahomes missed no regular-season games last year but the surgery raised cautious flags during the offseason program. Those concerns now appear fully put to rest. The Chiefs also received news elsewhere that former quarterback Will Grier is returning to the Cowboys organization as an offensive assistant, according to a source, adding yet another familiar name to the NFL coaching carousel this summer.

secondary.headline: ROCKIES STUN BREWERS AGAIN, 5-2, TO TAKE 2-0 SERIES ADVANTAGE
secondary.deck: Colorado builds lead early in Milwaukee, silences American Family Field crowd of 37,089
secondary.body:
MILWAUKEE -- The Colorado Rockies, owners of one of the worst records in the National League at 42-63, are making no apologies. Colorado stunned the first-place Milwaukee Brewers for the second straight day Friday, rolling to a 5-2 victory at American Family Field before 37,089 to take a 2-0 series lead against a Brewers club that entered at 64-39 and atop the NL Central.

Colorado struck for two runs in the first inning and added single tallies in the third and fourth to build a 4-1 cushion before the capacity crowd fully processed what was happening. The Rockies tacked on an insurance run in the seventh, with a pinch-hit double by a reserve coming in that frame, while Milwaukee managed only a run in the first and another in the sixth. The loss was a quiet embarrassment for a Brewers team with playoff aspirations, and Colorado showed no signs of wilting despite its lowly standing in the NL West.

column.headline: CROW-ARMSTRONG IS FOR REAL, AND THE CUBS SHOULD DARE TO DREAM
column.body:
Twenty-two home runs before the calendar hits August is not a coincidence. Pete Crow-Armstrong is doing something special in Chicago this summer, and Friday night in Pittsburgh was the clearest proof yet. When the Cubs needed one swing in extras to escape PNC Park with a win, their young outfielder supplied it without flinching. That is not a fluke. That is a centerpiece building.

The Cubs have spent years searching for the kind of player who changes a franchise's ceiling. Crow-Armstrong, with his bat and his instincts, looks more and more like that player every week. If Chicago's front office can surround him properly, this team is not merely competitive. It is dangerous. The rest of the National League would be wise to start paying attention.

story.headline: BRAVES RALLY IN TENTH TO EDGE ORIOLES IN THRILLER, 7-6
story.deck: Atlanta explodes for four runs in extras to escape Baltimore with a hard-fought victory.
story.body:
BALTIMORE, July 25 — The Atlanta Braves turned a tense, back-and-forth ballgame into a road victory Friday night, scoring four times in the tenth inning to defeat the Baltimore Orioles 7-6 before 35,775 at Camden Yards. The Braves entered extras tied at three apiece, then broke the game open against an Orioles bullpen that had held Atlanta scoreless through the sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth. A sacrifice fly from Holliday capped the decisive rally and sent the Braves home with the win.

The long ball fueled most of the scoring on both sides. Matt Olson crushed his 27th home run of the season for Atlanta, while C.J. Encarnacion-Strand added his third of the year and also doubled. Baldwin went deep for his 20th of the season for the Braves. Baltimore kept pace through nine innings, with the Orioles stranding a staggering 20 runners on base, a number that ultimately told the story of a night full of missed opportunities for the home club.

The loss dropped Baltimore, sitting fourth in the AL East at 50-54, further from a postseason position, while the first-place Braves at 61-42 extended their grip on the NL East. In other action Friday, the Tampa Bay Rays pounded Cleveland 11-3 as Nick Fortes finished with two doubles in a 22-runner left-on-base performance by Tampa Bay, and Paul Goldschmidt's 16th home run stood as the lone run in New York's 1-0 shutout of Philadelphia.

story.headline: LEBRON JAMES JOINS THE 76ERS, SENDING PHILADELPHIA INTO AN ALL-OUT FRENZY
story.deck: LeBron's stunning move to Philly pairs him with Joel Embiid in a championship-or-bust gamble.
story.body:
Philadelphia erupted Friday as LeBron James officially agreed to join the 76ers, sending shockwaves through the NBA landscape and transforming a franchise that has spent years agonizing over what might have been into an immediate title contender. ESPN's Kevin Negandhi called it an incredible day to be a 76ers fan, and the city of Philadelphia, starved for a basketball championship, appeared to agree. James, 41, becomes the most decorated free agent signing in franchise history, bringing four championships, four MVP awards, and an unmatched basketball IQ to a roster already anchored by a healthy Joel Embiid.

The pairing of James and Embiid figures to dominate the Eastern Conference conversation from now through next June, but ESPN's Michael Wilbon wasted no time placing the burden of expectation squarely on the seven-footer from Cameroon. Wilbon argued Friday that Embiid, not James, must now deliver the defining performances when the playoffs arrive, suggesting that LeBron's presence removes every remaining excuse for Philly's franchise center. Embiid has never advanced past the second round, and with James alongside him, that ceiling will no longer be accepted as a reasonable outcome by fans, ownership, or the broader basketball world.

The move does carry significant fantasy basketball implications, according to ESPN analysts tracking the offseason. James' ball-dominant style figures to compress usage for Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and the rest of the supporting cast, diminishing individual statistical value even as the team's collective championship odds soar. Brian Windhorst, whose Hoop Collective podcast has been tracking every ripple of this deal for weeks, reported that additional roster moves remain in motion as Philadelphia works to build the right complement around its two megastars before training camp opens this fall.

story.headline: GRANATO STEPS BACK AS CANUCKS SHAKE UP FRONT OFFICE AMID BUSY SUMMER AROUND THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Hockey Hall of Famer shifts to adviser role while Columbus makes bold moves up front
story.body:
Cammi Granato, the Hockey Hall of Fame forward whose groundbreaking career helped reshape women's hockey, is stepping away from her role as assistant general manager of the Vancouver Canucks and moving into an advisory position, the team confirmed Saturday. The transition marks a significant front-office shift for a Canucks organization still searching for the right front-office formula after years of organizational turbulence. Granato had joined the Canucks in 2021 as one of the first women to hold an assistant GM title in NHL history.

While Vancouver restructures, the Columbus Blue Jackets were busy making noise on two fronts Friday. The club locked up forward Cole Sillinger to a three-year contract, avoiding what would have been a contentious arbitration hearing for the 22-year-old center, who has shown flashes of the offensive upside that made him a first-round pick in 2021. Hours later, Columbus announced it had signed goaltender Jet Greaves to a three-year, $15 million deal running through the 2028-29 season, signaling a firm commitment to the young netminder as the franchise cornerstone between the pipes.

Meanwhile, John Tortorella told reporters he was flat-out disappointed when the Vegas Golden Knights chose not to retain him following their surprising playoff run, a stunning rebuke of a coach who has won a Jack Adams Award and built a reputation as one of the game's fiercest motivators. Tortorella, 67, said he remains eager for his next opportunity and expects interest to follow. With several NHL benches potentially opening before training camps begin in September, it is unlikely the combustible and accomplished coach will remain on the sidelines for long.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILD AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Veteran signal-callers change addresses while draft picks settle into new homes across the league.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback shuffle, with several franchises overhauling their rosters just months after the Los Angeles Rams hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at Super Bowl LX. The Cleveland Browns, desperate to end years of mediocrity, agreed to terms with veteran quarterback Russell Wilson on a two-year deal worth $42 million, betting the 37-year-old still has enough left in the tank to stabilize a franchise that has cycled through starters at an alarming rate. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders swung a blockbuster trade with the New England Patriots, acquiring second-year passer Drake Maye in exchange for two first-round picks and a package of veteran talent that gutted the Silver and Black's depth chart overnight.

The 2026 NFL Draft produced its share of instant storylines, none larger than Colorado wide receiver and Heisman finalist Tetairoa McMillan landing with the Dallas Cowboys at pick seven, giving quarterback Dak Prescott a legitimate field-stretching weapon to pair with CeeDee Lamb. Draft analysts at NFL Network called the selection the best value of the first round, pointing to McMillan's 4.38 speed and exceptional hands as traits that translate immediately at the professional level. The Tennessee Titans, picking second overall, selected Oregon offensive tackle Emeka Egbuka to anchor a rebuilt line around second-year starter Will Levis.

Training camps remain two months away, but front offices are burning the phones. The Philadelphia Eagles restructured Jalen Hurts's contract to clear $18 million in cap space, then used the flexibility to sign Pro Bowl cornerback Sauce Gardner away from the Jets on a five-year deal that immediately vaults Philadelphia back into the NFC title conversation. Eagles general manager Howie Roseman, never shy about making noise in the offseason, called Gardner the final piece of a defense built to carry the franchise deep into January. Jets fans, still stinging from the trade, flooded social media with frustration as New York begins yet another painful rebuild.
